newsitem.title: UK: Spain sets first Bono-exchangeable Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Spain sets first Bono-exchangeable Eurobond.

text.p: Spain on Thursday launched its first Eurobond which will be exchangeable, after EMU, into a domestic government bond issue, joint lead manager SBC Warburg said on Thursday.

The 1.25 billion euro deal, due January 31, 2008, will be mandatorily exchangeable into a six percent strippable Spanish government bond of the same maturity after both bonds' January 31, 1999 coupon date.
The euro deal, on which Banco Central Hispano, Paribas and Santander de Negocios were also joint lead managers, will be priced later to yield 15 basis points over French Ecu OATs.
French and Spanish benchmark 10-year bonds, denominated in francs and pesetas respectively, were trading at a spread of 77 b.p. at 0830 GMT.

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
From that date, all national currencies within the euro area will cease to exist legally and will instead be expressions of the euro.
